message:
## Vulnerability Digest

Daily sweep for the Products.txt list, covering credible public vulnerability reports and material advisory updates observed in the last 24 hours before the scheduled run on 2026-07-30 05:10 IST. Confirmed relevant updates were found for VMware ESXi/vCenter, Ubuntu, Samba, and NGINX. No fresh credible findings were confirmed for the other monitored products in this window.

**Finding 1**

- Product: VMware ESXi / VMware vCenter
- Issue: VMSA-2026-0006: CVE-2026-59309, CVE-2026-59310, CVE-2026-47876, CVE-2026-41703, and CVE-2026-41709
- Severity: Critical overall; Broadcom lists a CVSSv3 range of 2.7-9.8.
- Description: Broadcom published updates for multiple VMware ESX, vCenter, Workstation, and Fusion vulnerabilities. The highest-impact issues include vCenter authentication bypass and directory traversal flaws rated up to CVSS 9.8, plus an ESX VMXNET3 out-of-bounds write rated up to CVSS 9.3.
- Why it appears relevant: Products.txt includes VMware ESXi and VMware vCenter, and the Broadcom advisory explicitly lists VMware vSphere ESXi and VMware vCenter Server among affected products.
- Source: Broadcom VMSA-2026-0006 https://support.broadcom.com/web/ecx/support-content-notification/-/external/content/SecurityAdvisories/0/38017

**Finding 2**

- Product: Ubuntu / Linux kernel
- Issue: Ubuntu Security Notices USN-8623-1, USN-8622-1, USN-8620-2, and USN-8615-2
- Severity: Not clearly stated as a single severity in the Ubuntu notices.
- Description: Ubuntu published July 29 notices for Linux kernel variants, including NVIDIA, Azure FIPS, and Raspberry Pi kernel packages. The notices describe kernel flaws that could potentially allow system compromise, privilege escalation, container escape, denial of service, or information disclosure depending on the CVE and kernel flavor.
- Why it appears relevant: Products.txt includes Ubuntu, and the notices explicitly apply to supported Ubuntu releases including 18.04 LTS, 20.04 LTS, 22.04 LTS, 24.04 LTS, and/or 26.04 LTS depending on the notice.
- Source: Ubuntu Security Notices https://ubuntu.com/security/notices; USN-8622-1 https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8622-1; USN-8615-2 https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8615-2

**Finding 3**

- Product: Samba / CIFS-SMB services
- Issue: USN-8621-1 and Debian DSA-6401-1 for Samba vulnerabilities: CVE-2026-6949, CVE-2026-58216, CVE-2026-58218, CVE-2026-58221, CVE-2026-58222, CVE-2026-58224, plus CVE-2026-15779 in Ubuntu
- Severity: Not clearly stated as a single severity in the Ubuntu or Debian advisory.
- Description: The Samba advisories cover denial of service, information disclosure, privilege escalation, and an authenticated LDAP issue that could permit unauthorized modifications and domain takeover.
- Why it appears relevant: Products.txt includes Samba and CIFS/SMB Utils. Ubuntu describes the package as an SMB/CIFS file, print, and login server for Unix, and Debian likewise identifies the affected package as Samba.
- Source: Ubuntu USN-8621-1 https://ubuntu.com/security/notices/USN-8621-1; Debian DSA-6401-1 https://lists.debian.org/debian-security-announce/2026/msg00312.html; Samba advisory archive example https://www.samba.org/samba/security/CVE-2026-58224-advisory.html

**Finding 4**

- Product: NGINX
- Issue: Existing NGINX CVEs with fresh exploit-development/public-coverage activity: CVE-2026-42533, plus related July NGINX fixes CVE-2026-60005 and CVE-2026-56434
- Severity: NGINX rates CVE-2026-42533 as major, CVE-2026-60005 as medium, and CVE-2026-56434 as medium.
- Description: NGINX 1.30.4 and 1.31.3 fix a map/regex buffer overflow, a slice-module memory disclosure issue, and an SSI-module use-after-free. The vulnerabilities were originally patched earlier in July, but public reporting in the current window noted exploit-development activity for CVE-2026-42533.
- Why it appears relevant: Products.txt includes Nginx, and the official NGINX advisory page explicitly lists the affected NGINX Open Source and NGINX Plus vulnerabilities. The fresh element is public exploit-development coverage, not the original disclosure date.
- Source: NGINX advisories https://nginx.org/en/security_advisories.html; The Hacker News update https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/critical-nginx-vulnerability-can-crash.html

**Possible matches needing review**

- Google Chrome / ChromeOS: Google published Chrome and ChromeOS channel updates on July 29. The page lists explicit selected security fixes for ChromeOS LTS, while the desktop Chrome entry did not enumerate CVEs in the captured page text. Treat this as a browser update to review for Chrome fleets, but not a fully detailed confirmed vulnerability finding for desktop Google Chrome. Source: https://chromereleases.googleblog.com/
- MongoDB: Recent search results surfaced MongoDB Server, Atlas Search, and Ops Manager CVEs, but the credible dates observed were May 2026 or July 22-23, outside this 24-hour window. No MongoDB-family item was included as a confirmed new finding for this run.

Closing note: Immediate review is recommended for VMware ESXi/vCenter because Broadcom published critical vCenter and ESX issues on July 29. NGINX deployments below 1.30.4 or 1.31.3 should also be checked because public exploit-development coverage is circulating. Ubuntu kernel and Samba updates should be reviewed through the normal Linux patch process.
